correctness.rationale: At fixed 0<s<1, direct differentiation gives the trace mu and determinant s^2 and the stated scaled oscillator. Independently set q=r cos(theta), p=−r sin(theta), with G=q'−p in scaled time. Then r'=cos(theta)G and theta'=1−sin(theta)G/r. Writing c=cos(theta), v=sin(theta), the order-two and order-three parts of G/r are r g2 and r^2 g3 with g2=A c^2−Bcv, g3=C c^3−D c^2v and A,B,C,D as in RESULT.md. At mu=0 the mean cubic radial return term is (3C−AB)/8=−1/(8s^3): the term from varying r in the quadratic radial term integrates to zero because that primitive U has U(0)=U(2pi)=0. In the travel time per turn the linear term averages to zero, as does the term linear in mu; the quadratic coefficient is the mean of v g3+v^2 g2^2+U v g2 with U=A(v−v^3/3)+(B/3)(c^3−1). The three means are −D/8, (A^2+B^2)/16, and (5A^2−B^2)/48. Their sum is (9s^4−5s^2+1)/(24s^4). The linear radial growth has slope 1/(2s) in scaled time, hence along the stable Hopf cycle r^2 is 4s^2 mu to leading order. The analytic remainder can be justified by the analytic signed-section return map, dividing its fixed-point displacement by the initial radius and applying the implicit function theorem in mu. Half return interchanges the two signed section crossings as an analytic involution with derivative −1. In the odd coordinate induced by this involution both mu and the return time are even analytic, and mu has nonzero quadratic coefficient. Thus the remainder is O_s(mu^2). Monotone angle on the small branch makes one turn its least period; physical time divides scaled time by s. The normalized slope simplifies to [1+(3s−1/s)^2]/6, with equality only at 1/sqrt(3). Local nondegenerate supercritical Hopf supplies uniqueness and orbital asymptotic stability. No uniformity in s or global period law is needed. Inspected both frozen scripts without executing them; this independent return calculation is analytical rather than numerical shooting.

evidence: The 2013 model includes diffusion, but its j=0 spatially homogeneous Hopf branch is exactly the same ODE; Theorem 2.2 gives its stable supercritical branch for the entire range 0<s<1.

evidence: Let b0'=(1−3s^2)/2. In the 2013 convention their projections give g20=−b0'−2is, g11=−b0', g21=−3s^2+is, with zero corrections from the two displayed homogeneous center-manifold terms. The projection of the real forcing direction (1,−1) is real, so g02 is the conjugate of g20.

Substituting into c1=i(g20*g11−2|g11|^2−|g02|^2/3)/(2s)+g21/2 gives Re c1=−1/2 and Im c1=s/2−2[(b0')^2+s^2]/(3s)=−(9s^4−5s^2+1)/(6s). This uses their exact displayed complex data, not only their stability sign.

The real eigenvalue part is mu/2 and the linear imaginary part is sqrt(s^2−mu^2/4)=s+O_s(mu^2). Consequently the leading squared normal-form radius is mu and the angular frequency is s+(Im c1)mu+O_s(mu^2). Expanding the reciprocal gives the frozen normalized slope. Completing the square gives 1/6 and its unique minimizer.
